questions.question: What is JavaScript used for in web development?
questions.explanation: JavaScript makes web pages interactive — handling clicks, form validation, animations, dynamic content changes.

questions.question: Which keyword should you use to declare a variable that won't change?
questions.explanation: Use 'const' for values that won't change. Use 'let' only when the value needs to change. Avoid 'var'.

questions.question: What does === check in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: === (strict equality) checks both value AND type. '5' === 5 is false (string vs number). Always use === over ==.

questions.question: What is the output of: console.log(typeof 42)?
questions.explanation: JavaScript has only one number type called 'number' — no separate integer or float types.

questions.question: How do you add an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: array.push(item) adds an item to the end. array.pop() removes the last item.

questions.question: What is a template literal in JavaScript?
options: A string using backticks with ${} for variables
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks (`) and ${variable} for easy string building: `Hello, ${name}!`

questions.question: What does document.querySelector('.card') select?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns the FIRST matching element. Use querySelectorAll to get ALL matching elements.

questions.question: How many columns does Bootstrap's grid system have?
questions.explanation: Bootstrap divides the page into 12 columns. col-6 = 50% width, col-4 = 33.3%, col-3 = 25%.

questions.question: Which Bootstrap class creates a blue button?
questions.explanation: btn-primary creates a blue button. Bootstrap uses color names: primary (blue), success (green), danger (red).

questions.question: What does 'col-md-6' mean in Bootstrap?
options: 6 columns wide on medium screens and up
questions.explanation: col-md-6 means take 6 out of 12 columns (50% width) on medium screens (768px) and up.

questions.question: Which array method creates a new array by transforming each item?
questions.explanation: map() creates a new array by applying a function to each item. [1,2,3].map(x => x*2) returns [2,4,6].

questions.question: What is the arrow function syntax for: function add(a,b) { return a+b; }?
questions.explanation: Arrow functions: const add = (a, b) => a + b; Shorter syntax for simple functions.
